title: Commercial Lease Expiring Soon? A Newcastle Tenant’s Next-Step Checklist
excerpt: When the lease deadline is close, focus on verified dates, clear responsibilities and realistic options. Use this checklist to prepare a useful conversation about renewal or relocation.
metaTitle: Commercial Lease Expiring Soon Newcastle | YOS
metaDescription: Lease expiry approaching? Organise confirmed dates, documents, renewal options and relocation constraints before your Newcastle business makes its next lease decision.
author: Joe Kelley
body:
## What should you do if your commercial lease expires soon?

Start with the actual lease documents and the decision that needs attention first. An approaching expiry can limit planning time, but it does not establish that every option is lost or that a particular rent outcome is achievable. Your circumstances, lease provisions and available premises need to be assessed.

For a Newcastle or Hunter business, a useful first brief records the premises, confirmed dates, business requirements and unresolved questions. You do not need to decide to move before asking for help.

## Confirm the dates before planning around them

Gather the signed lease, amendments and recent landlord correspondence. Ask your solicitor to confirm expiry, any relevant notice requirements and the status of any option. Do not rely on a generic 60-day or 12-month rule from an article.

Use the [critical dates tool](/tools/critical-dates) to organise confirmed information. Keep uncertain dates marked as questions until the appointed adviser checks them.

**Helpful tip:** distinguish a requested response date in correspondence from a confirmed requirement in your documents. Ask your solicitor what each means for your situation.

## Assemble a brief that someone can act on

| Information | What to gather | Why it helps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lease position | Documents, correspondence and confirmed dates | Establishes the questions and decisions that need attention |
| Current costs | Rent, available outgoings information and proposed terms | Creates a consistent commercial starting point |
| Business requirements | Team attendance, activities, access and essential location needs | Helps test staying and moving against the same brief |
| Transition constraints | Existing items to retain, IT needs, fit out and operating limits | Makes relocation dependencies visible |
| Decision owners | People who approve terms, expenditure and appointments | Reduces avoidable delays in the decision process |

If a document is missing, record who may hold it and who will request it. Avoid treating an unverified assumption as an approved instruction.

## Test renewal and relocation without assuming the answer

For a renewal, record what works in the current premises, what needs changing and the proposed commercial terms. For relocation, include the steps required to find, assess, prepare and occupy another property.

Compare ongoing occupancy costs separately from moving, initial works, furniture, possible overlap and existing lease exit obligations. Any market comparisons should identify their evidence, date and limitations; an advertised asking rent alone does not establish a completed deal or a guaranteed negotiating result.

[Compare renewing with relocating](/blog/renew-or-relocate-commercial-lease)

[Organise lease assumptions in the comparison tool](/resources/lease-comparison)

## Make the delivery constraints visible

A property that appears suitable may still need investigations, landlord inputs, design decisions, appointed contractors, furniture or IT work before the team can operate. Ask the relevant advisers to identify the actual dependencies rather than assuming a move can fit the remaining time.

YOS can connect the leasing brief with [client-side office FitOut planning](/office-fitout) where agreed. Construction and trade work remains with appointed contractors; YOS's management scope is agreed separately.

**Helpful tip:** write down the date the business needs to operate and the decisions that must precede it. Flag any period when continuity across two sites may need planning.

## Keep advice and authority clear

Your solicitor advises on legal terms, notices and documentation. YOS supports the agreed tenant-side commercial brief, options and negotiation workstream. Confirm scope, fees and any relevant third-party payment arrangements before engagement.

A short remaining timeframe does not make savings, an extension or alternative premises certain. The purpose of an initial conversation is to understand the situation and establish a realistic next step.

## Start with the dates and decision you know
